definitions.explanation: During the Edo period, warehouses maintained by feudal domains in major commercial cities, especially Osaka, to store and sell rice and other products from their territories.

examples.japanese: {大阪|おおさか}には{多|おお}くの{蔵屋敷|くらやしき}があった。
examples.english: There were many domain warehouses in Osaka.

examples.japanese: {各藩|かくはん}は{蔵屋敷|くらやしき}を{通|つう}じて{年貢米|ねんぐまい}を{売|う}りさばいた。
examples.english: Each domain sold its tax rice through its warehouse estate.

examples.japanese: {蔵屋敷|くらやしき}は{藩|はん}の{経済|けいざい}を{支|ささ}える{重要|じゅうよう}な{拠点|きょてん}であり、{大阪|おおさか}が「{天下|てんか}の{台所|だいどころ}」と{呼|よ}ばれる{理由|りゆう}の{一|ひと}つだった。
examples.english: Domain warehouses were important bases supporting each domain's economy, and were one of the reasons Osaka was called 'the kitchen of the nation.'

notes:
CULTURE:
A key institution of Edo-period commercial life. Osaka, as the center of rice trading, had the highest concentration of {蔵屋敷|くらやしき}. Each feudal domain ({藩|はん}) maintained one or more of these in Osaka or Edo to convert their rice tax ({年貢|ねんぐ}) into cash. The {蔵屋敷|くらやしき} system contributed to the development of Japan's early commodity markets.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大阪|おおさか}の{蔵屋敷|くらやしき} (Osaka domain warehouses)
- {藩|はん}の{蔵屋敷|くらやしき} (a domain's warehouse estate)
- {蔵屋敷|くらやしき}{跡|あと} (site of a former domain warehouse)
